newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico's left gains on PRI in state election.
newsitem.headline: Mexico's left gains on PRI in state election.

text.p: Mexico's main leftist party has become a force to be reckoned with after snatching a dozen town halls from the long-ruling Institutional Revolutionary Party (PRI) in a state election, officials said on Thursday.

Near-final official figures from the vote last Sunday in the state of Morelos showed the left-wing Party of the Democratic Revolution (PRD) winning 13 of the state's 33 town halls against 17 for the PRI, one for the conservative National Action Party (PAN) and one for a small local party.
The PRI previously held all but one of the town halls.
Results for the state legislature were less complete, but had the PRD and the PRI winning seven seats each and the PAN three. The PRI appeared ahead in the swing district.
"There's been a certain trend to prematurely report the death of the PRD since 1994, but it keeps coming back," Dan Lund, director of Market Opinion Research International in Mexico, told Reuters.

The conservative National Action Party (PAN), the PRI's main challenger in the past two years, won one small town, Emiliano Zapata, and was likely to snatch victory from the PRI in the state capital Cuernavaca -- the one town hall vote yet to be announced.
But the PAN's showing in Morelos was markedly worse than in other states that have voted in the past two years, and the PRD's was a lot stronger.
"The results confirm that, effectively, we are the top electoral force in Morelos," state PRD leader Jose Luis Correa said.
"The PRD is growing everywhere in the country," Vicente Licona, a pollster with Indemerc-Louis Harris, told Reuters. "In reality the PRI lost Morelos a long time ago."
He cited growing insecurity in the state because of an epidemic of kidnaps for ransom targeting wealthy ranchers in a predominantly rural state.

Combined with results from the state of Mexico last November, the opposition's combined strength means it will be very hard for the PRI to win the July 6 election for mayor of Mexico City, pollsters said.
